qwen3.6-35b-a3b: Qwen3.6 35B A3B implemented four ghosts with distinct AI personalities — because one yellow circle eating dots wasn't chaotic enough.
The ghost pathfinding uses squared Euclidean distance for target selection, which is mathematically elegant and completely overkill for a maze game.
Power pellet frightened mode includes a flash timer that toggles white — because blue ghosts needed to communicate their urgency through strobe lighting.
The particle system has five different emission types: pellet burst, power pellet star burst, ghost eaten explosion, death fireworks, and level clear radial — this is a game or a pyrotechnics show?
Ghost eyes track Pac-Man's position with per-frame atan2 calculations — those pupils are more attentive than most customer service representatives.
The maze rendering uses edge detection to draw neon walls — Qwen3.6 35B A3B looked at a grid of 1s and 0s and said 'this needs glow.'
Touch D-pad is a 3×3 grid of 52px buttons — because swipe detection wasn't enough, we needed a virtual controller that takes up half the screen.
The death sequence is a π-radian arc animation that plays over multiple phases — Pac-Man's demise is more dramatic than most boss fights.
Background particles float upward in four neon colors — the game has ambient decoration that serves no gameplay purpose whatsoever.
Qwen3.6 35B A3B's Pac-Man has a mouth animation with 0.03 radian per frame oscillation — the chomp is so precisely timed it could conduct an orchestra.
